docs: This starts an animation of a node property according to the specified parameters. If the node property is already being animated, that animation will be canceled and replaced by the new one. Note however that several different node properties can be animated simultaneously. Use `gui.cancel_animations` to stop the animation before it has completed. Only the node properties gui.get lists can be animated; a material constant cannot. Composite properties of type vector3, vector4 or quaternion also expose their sub-components (x, y, z and w). You can address the components individually by suffixing the name with a dot '.' and the name of the component. For instance, `"position.x"` (the position x coordinate) or `"color.w"` (the color alpha value). If a `complete_function` (Lua function) is specified, that function will be called when the animation has completed. By starting a new animation in that function, several animations can be sequenced together. See the examples below for more information.

Animates a node property named by a hash whose name is not known at compile time, such as a bare `Hash`. The engine resolves the name at run time, so the target value is not checked against the property: pass a number, a vmath.vector3, a vmath.vector4 or a vmath.quat as the named property expects. A hash of a node property name, such as `hash("position.y")`, takes what that name takes.

docs:
Instead of using specific getters such as gui.get_position or gui.get_scale, you can use gui.get instead and supply the property as a string, a `gui.PROP_*` constant or a hash of the name. Only these node properties are supported:

- `"position"`
- `"rotation"`
- `"euler"`
- `"scale"`
- `"color"`
- `"outline"`
- `"shadow"`
- `"size"`
- `"fill_angle"` (pie)
- `"inner_radius"` (pie)
- `"leading"` (text)
- `"tracking"` (text)
- `"slice9"` (slice9)

Each property but the four scalars (`fill_angle`, `inner_radius`, `leading` and `tracking`) also exposes its components as `"<name>.x"` to `"<name>.w"`. Getting `"rotation"` returns a vmath.quat, another vector property a vmath.vector4, and a component or a scalar property a single number. To get a material constant, pass its name as a hash.

Gets a material constant of a node, or a property named by a hash whose name is not known at compile time, such as a bare `Hash`. Pass the constant's name as a hash, such as `hash("tint")`. A hash of a node property name, such as `hash("position")`, reads as that name does. Reading an array constant without `index` returns every element in a table.

A hash of a node property name, such as `hash("position")`, reads as that name does. Reading an array constant without `index` returns every element in a table.
Gets a node property named by a value that may be either a property name or a hash, such as one typed `"position" | Hash`. The result is any value either form returns; narrow it before use.

docs:
Instead of using specific setters such as gui.set_position or gui.set_scale, you can use gui.set instead and supply the property as a string, a `gui.PROP_*` constant or a hash of the name. Only the node properties gui.get lists are supported.

The value depends on the property name. Setting `"rotation"` takes a vmath.quat, which differs from gui.set_rotation; to set the rotation in degrees, set `"euler"` instead. The rotation and euler properties are linked, so changing one changes the other. Every other vector property takes a vmath.vector4 or a vmath.vector3, and a component such as `"position.x"` or one of the four scalar properties takes a single number.

Sets a material constant of a node, or a property named by a hash whose name is not known at compile time, such as a bare `Hash`; a hash of a node property name, such as `hash("position")`, takes what that name takes. If a material specifies a constant called `tint` in the .material file, set it with `gui.set(node, hash("tint"), vmath.vector4(1, 0, 0, 1))`, or pass a vmath.matrix4 if the constant is a matrix. To set one element of an array constant, pass an options table with `index` set.

To set one element of an array constant, pass an options table with `index` set.
